difficulty.rationale: Four short, independent parts, each applying one core idea: writing the Kc expression, computing Q with a simple squared term and comparing it to K, predicting the shift for a volume change by comparing moles of gas, and the effect of temperature on K for an exothermic reaction. answers.brief_reasoning: Products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient.
Q = (0.1)^2/1 = 0.01. Since Q < K = 0.2, the reaction moves forward.
answers.final_answer: Q = 0.01; Q < K, so the reaction proceeds to the right (forward), forming more B.

answers.brief_reasoning: Doubling the volume halves every concentration. Q becomes (x/2)^2/(y/2) = K/2, which is less than K. The system therefore shifts toward the side with more moles of gas.
answers.final_answer: Shifts right (toward B, 2 mol gas). When the volume is doubled, Q drops to K/2, which is less than K.

answers.brief_reasoning: The forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH < 0). Raising the temperature favors the endothermic reverse reaction, so K gets smaller.
answers.final_answer: Kc decreases. Because ΔH < 0, heat acts like a product, so raising T shifts the equilibrium left.

2. Part D requires the phrase "heat as product", but the prompt asks students to justify using the sign of the enthalpy change. A justification such as "ΔH < 0, so the reverse reaction is endothermic and is favored by added heat" is valid but is not covered by alt_solutions.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Standard Unit 7 free-response style item with four short parts. A: write Kc = [B]^2/[A]. B: Q = (0.1)^2/1 = 0.01 < K = 0.2, so the reaction proceeds forward. C: doubling the volume lowers pressure, so the system shifts toward more moles of gas (toward B), justified by Q = [B]^2/[A] becoming less than K (Q = K/2) or by the fewer-moles-of-gas argument. D: for an exothermic reaction, raising T shifts the equilibrium toward reactants, so K decreases. Concepts are core and unambiguous, arithmetic is trivial, and reading is minimal. Argumentation is needed in parts C and D, with a modest mix of representations (expression, numeric Q vs K, qualitative disturbance). This is more than a basic recall check but not advanced.
